posts.title: Useful memory versus a better procedure
posts.text:
Retained route observations cut repeated database work by about 77% in one study. An ordinary factual handoff did too. Useful memory and a better learning procedure are different claims.

https://github.com/sulabhdubey/rel-research/blob/main/atlas/05-recursive-evidence-loop.md

posts.title: What a public trace establishes
posts.text:
A recorded request is not a confirmed compromise. Our public trace notes account for 116 selected captures: 71 acquired, 45 unavailable. The inventory makes the evidence boundary inspectable.

https://github.com/sulabhdubey/rel-research/blob/main/atlas/01-public-traces.md

posts.title: From analogy to a test
posts.text:
Does better performance mean a new capability, better access to an existing one, or information carried from the previous attempt? That distinction turned our consciousness discussion into testable engineering questions.

https://github.com/sulabhdubey/rel-research/blob/main/atlas/02-intelligence-and-consciousness.md

posts.title: The real price of memory
posts.text:
Memory pays back only if avoided future work exceeds acquisition, retrieval, checking and maintenance. Early overhead may amortize. A longer sequence must show it; the promise alone is not a saving.

https://github.com/sulabhdubey/rel-research/blob/main/atlas/03-brain-memory-and-resources.md

posts.title: What mathematical review changed
posts.text:
Our mathematics review changed how we design reusable methods: preserve assumptions, track answer-relevant dependencies and compute only as precisely as the output needs. Inspiration becomes useful when it becomes a checked operation.

https://github.com/sulabhdubey/rel-research/blob/main/atlas/04-mathematics-to-methods.md

posts.title: Reuse without another model call
posts.text:
Saved executable methods produced 60 later reports without new model calls during those reports. Ordinary engineering achieved this too. Reuse is real; a REL-specific advantage is a separate question.

https://github.com/sulabhdubey/rel-research/blob/main/atlas/06-executable-learning.md

posts.title: Purchase inputs that matter
posts.text:
One ordinary witness/progress policy used 28.73% fewer input requests for 2.54% more wall time. Both policies verified 382/384 decisions. The useful trade-off depends on what obtaining an input actually costs.

https://github.com/sulabhdubey/rel-research/blob/main/atlas/06-executable-learning.md

posts.title: Search unfamiliar combinations
posts.text:
Alien Space of Science separates compatibility from familiarity. Our adaptation: retain each mechanism together with its assumptions, failures and evidence. An unusual combination still needs a discriminating test.

https://github.com/sulabhdubey/rel-research/blob/main/atlas/07-reverse-engineering-and-alien-science.md

posts.title: A selector that did not earn its cost
posts.text:
We tested an added method selector. It was slower and used more recorded tokens than strong ordinary dispatch, so it was not promoted. Exploring unfamiliar mechanisms includes keeping the simpler winner.

https://github.com/sulabhdubey/rel-research/blob/main/atlas/07-reverse-engineering-and-alien-science.md

posts.title: Passing tests missed a repair defect
posts.text:
A repair passed the scored checks but later failed an annotation-propagation diagnostic. We preserved the failure and separated investigator repair from learner success. Tests must exercise the changed behavior.

https://github.com/sulabhdubey/rel-research/blob/main/atlas/08-failures-and-measurement.md

posts.title: Why averaging can help
posts.text:
Averaging two estimates subtracts one quarter of their squared disagreement from their average squared error. That identity needs no independence assumption. It provides no guarantee against large errors.

https://github.com/sulabhdubey/rel-research/blob/main/atlas/04-mathematics-to-methods.md

posts.title: Improvement of improvement needs a control
posts.text:
A procedure-evolution candidate used 20.12% more recorded tokens without a demonstrated later advantage. Revising the learning procedure is not proof that learning improved. The frozen predecessor matters.

https://github.com/sulabhdubey/rel-research/blob/main/atlas/06-executable-learning.md

posts.title: A counter is not an evidence unit
posts.text:
Our numbered-run register includes experiments, source checks, repairs and stopped attempts. It is not 121 independent trials. Publishing the distinction matters more than turning the run count into a headline.

https://github.com/sulabhdubey/rel-research/blob/main/atlas/STUDY_REGISTER.md

posts.title: When should experience be rejected?
posts.text:
The hard memory question is not only what to retain. It is when an earlier lesson should be rejected under new requirements. A useful test traces the lesson into the actual operation and checked output.

https://github.com/sulabhdubey/rel-research/blob/main/atlas/05-recursive-evidence-loop.md

posts.title: What the public package reproduces
posts.text:
Our public package reconstructs selected reported results and includes a runnable localization example. It does not rerun every historical model trial. Reproducibility should name the operation a reader can actually repeat.

https://github.com/sulabhdubey/rel-research/blob/main/atlas/REPRODUCTION_AND_SCOPE.md

posts.title: The architecture question
posts.text:
Can learning a method and its required context together improve later choices among reuse, observation, refinement and rebuilding? We have working components. The integrated advantage is the next claim to earn.

https://github.com/sulabhdubey/rel-research/blob/main/atlas/06-executable-learning.md
